textbookText: Take pyknometer and viscometer, wash with chromic acid followed by water and dry them.
Take the weight of empty and dry pyknometer. Fill with given liquid and water turn by turn and note down respective weight.
Clamp the viscometer vertically in the stand and attached rubber tube at the limb containing upper bulb.
Place certain volume of given liquid into limb containing lower bulb Suck up the liquid into upper bulb above upper mark. Keep liquid level stationary by holding rubber tube with finger.
Remove finger and start stop watch when liquid just crosses upper level and stop the watch as liquid come to lower mark.
Repeat this process three times for given liquid and carry out same process for water.

184 Practical Chemistry
EXPERIMENT NO. 14
Object: TO STUDY THE PROCESS OF ELECTROPLATING
APPRATUS REQUIRED
3. Iron nail
1. Voltameter
2. copper
4. Wire
5. Battery
CHEMICAL REQUIRED
CuS04 solution
THEORY

The process of chemical decomposition of electTolytic substance by passing current through it. The process of electrolysis can be applied for coaång desired metal on the surface of other metal. The metal to be coated is made as cathode and the metal by which the metal is coated is made as anode and salt of that metal is used as electrolyte. When current is passed through electrolyte. The metal ion from anode is migrated to cathode and deposited on surface by reduction.
Iron nail can be coated by copper by using CuS04 as electrolyte.
Ionization: cuS04 At anode At cathode AgN03 solution acidified with HN03 Copper (anode)
Iron (cathode) Figure6.5: Electroplating
Miscellaneous
PROCEDURE
1. Use a beaker as voltmeter and establish electric circuit by making
copper plate as anode and iron nail as cathode.
2. Take dil. CuS04 solution as electrolyte.
3. Connect circuit with battery.
4. Observe cathode and anode after sometime of experiment.
RESULT
Iron nail was coated with copper by the process of electroplating.
PRECAUTIONS
1. Two electrode should be sufficiently far apart.
2. Dilute solution should be used.
